sections.name: Summary Cards (renderSummary)
sections.data: Active picks count, closed count, win rate, total PnL, profit factor, expectancy, avg win/loss, proven vs probation breakdown. Includes live PnL cards when Binance API is reachable.
sections.reasoning: Core KPIs at a glance. Already filters by score tier and proven-only toggles. Could add Sharpe ratio card.

sections.name: Cross-System Agreement Matrix (renderAgreementMatrix)
sections.data: Grid of 23 tracked symbols x all systems. Shows LONG/SHORT arrows per system per symbol. Deduped by system groups. Includes credibility ranking, performance tooltips, forward validation.
sections.reasoning: Shows system-level consensus. Credibility-weighted ranking is good. The AGREE row at bottom provides actionable direction consensus. Strategy-level detail now in the new Strategy Consensus Matrix below it.

sections.name: Strategy Consensus Matrix (renderStrategyConsensus) -- NEW
sections.data: Groups active picks by symbol+direction, classifies each strategy as winner/loser/untracked based on closed trade WR. Shows conviction level (VERY_HIGH/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE). Entries with 0 winners collapsed.
sections.reasoning: Strategy-level consensus is the real signal. Shows which specific strategies with proven track records agree on a trade. Recency of last closed trade shown to detect stale strategies. Directly actionable for trade decisions.

sections.name: Overview Tab (renderOverview)
sections.data: Performance Breakdown (Proven/Sandbox/Probation/Demoted tiers), Asset Class Breakdown (Crypto/Forex/Equity), System Leaderboard (composite score ranking), Systems with Active Picks AND Positive History, Open Forward-Trades Live P/L by System.
sections.reasoning: The tier breakdown is critical -- shows proven systems at 50%+ WR vs sandbox dragging averages down. Composite ranking is modeled after CTA fund methodology. The 'Active + Positive History' table is immediately actionable.

sections.name: Active Picks Tab (renderPicks -- active)
sections.data: Full table of all currently open positions with symbol, direction, entry/TP/SL, PnL, score, confidence, strategy, system, trust tier, age. Filterable by system, asset class, direction, score tier.
sections.reasoning: Core trading view. Score column already uses composite scoring. Trust tier badges visible. Could add a 'strategy WR on this symbol' column to match SCM data.

sections.name: Closed Picks Tab (renderPicks -- closed)
sections.data: Recent closed trades with outcome, PnL, duration, strategy, system. Same filters as active.
sections.reasoning: Essential for tracking what worked. Duration data helps optimize hold times. Could add 'would this still be winning if held longer' analysis.

sections.name: Portfolios Tab (renderPortfolios + renderClaudePortfolios)
sections.data: Paper trading portfolios with equity curves, P/L, win rates, drawdowns. Claude's AI Portfolios with 4-AI consensus firewall. 12+ simulated portfolios including Prop Firm challenges.
sections.reasoning: Shows real-world portfolio impact of different strategy selections. Prop firm challenge tracking validates whether the system can pass funded account rules. Commission and slippage modeled.

sections.name: Dashboards Tab (renderDashboards)
sections.data: Links to all live dashboards (Audit, Alpha, KIMI, Monitor, Paper Trading, etc.). Discord channel configuration. Discord alert history.
sections.reasoning: Navigation hub. Useful for discovery but doesn't directly improve trade quality. Could add uptime monitoring for each dashboard URL.

sections.name: Systems Tab (renderSystems)
sections.data: Card grid of all trading systems with status, win rate, PnL, active/closed counts, probation status.
sections.reasoning: Gives system overview but doesn't break down to individual strategy performance within each system. The Leaderboard tab has more detail. Could merge or add strategy breakdown on click.

sections.name: BT vs Forward Tab (renderBtVsFwd)
sections.data: Table comparing backtest WR vs forward-test WR per strategy. Shows decay (FWD WR - BT WR). Sortable by any column.
sections.reasoning: Critical for detecting overfitting. Negative decay = strategy is overfit to historical data. This data should feed into the scoring formula to penalize strategies with large negative decay.

sections.name: Leaderboard Tab (renderLeaderboard)
sections.data: Strategy-level leaderboard with WR, PnL, trade count, profit factor. Filterable by system, sortable by any column.
sections.reasoning: Strategy-level granularity is exactly what's needed. Shows which specific algorithms perform best. Could add per-symbol breakdown and regime-specific performance.

sections.name: Bundles Tab (renderBundles)
sections.data: Strategy bundles (groups of strategies) with blended WR, total return, quality score. Forward-confirmed vs backtest-projected confidence levels.
sections.reasoning: Shows which strategy combinations work together. Quality score is useful but needs live paper-trading validation. Currently mostly backtest-projected.

sections.name: Permutations Tab (renderPermutations)
sections.data: System permutations and strategy permutations with trust levels, composite scores. Portfolio optimization via exhaustive combination testing. Best/worst system pairs.
sections.reasoning: Identifies best system pairs (e.g., momentum+trend+volume = 64% WR). The pair affinity data directly improves consensus scoring. Trust levels (highly_trusted, trusted) are actionable filters.

sections.name: Performance Tab (renderPerformance)
sections.data: 6 sections: (1) Score Band Analysis, (2) Confidence/Direction/Asset breakdowns, (3) Strategy-level P/L table with Sharpe estimates, (4) Cumulative PnL over time chart, (5) Score Accuracy Analysis (validates scoring formula), (6) Super Parameter Analysis with interactive filters, (7) Regime Validation (Mercury's Checklist).
sections.reasoning: The Score Accuracy Analysis is critical -- it validates whether the scoring formula actually predicts winners. The regime validation checks whether the regime meta-router improves trade selection. Mercury's 3-check framework (signal-to-trade ratio, regime-specific WR, max DD reduction) is rigorous.

sections.name: Warnings Tab (renderPicks -- warnings)
sections.data: Picks with warning flags (stale, conflicting signals, etc.)
sections.reasoning: Surfaces problematic picks that need attention. Should be more prominent when warnings exist.

sections.name: Audit Log Tab (renderAuditLog)
sections.data: Recent audit events (picks posted, TP/SL hits, reversals) and filter decisions (why picks were blocked/passed).
sections.reasoning: Raw event log is useful for debugging but not directly actionable for trading. Could aggregate: 'filter X blocked Y picks that would have been winners' to tune filters.

sections.name: Score Tracker Tab (renderScoreTracker)
sections.data: Snapshots top 10 scored picks every 10 minutes to localStorage. Tracks what-if P/L of high-scored picks over time.
sections.reasoning: Validates scoring in real-time. If high-score picks consistently move favorably, the scoring formula is working. Critical feedback loop for score tuning.

sections.name: ML Health Tab (renderMLHealth)
sections.data: ML system status cards showing model type, mode (active/heuristic/disabled), CV AUC, staleness, version.
sections.reasoning: Shows which ML models are functioning vs stale/disabled. AUC < 0.50 = anti-predictive and should be disabled. Staleness alerts prevent trading on outdated models.

sections.name: Claude Top Picks Tab (renderClaudeTopPicks)
sections.data: Claude's AI-selected top 3 picks with reasoning, live P/L tracking.
sections.reasoning: Interesting AI-curated view but needs 50+ closed picks to validate whether Claude's selection adds alpha over the scoring formula.

sections.name: 4-AI Battle Tab (renderAIBattle)
sections.data: Head-to-head comparison of 4 AI agents (Claude, Grok, Mercury, Codex) with independent picks and P/L tracking across multiple phases.
sections.reasoning: Novel approach to AI evaluation. Phase 1 showed all-SHORT bias. Phase 2 picks are fresh. Need 3+ phases with 50+ picks each to draw statistically significant conclusions about which AI is best at pick selection.
